models.name: Daily conversation
models.about: Everyday English: talking about your day, plans, likes and simple stories.

questions.q: Tell me about your typical day.
questions.tip: Go in time order: morning, afternoon, evening. Use linking words like first, after that, finally.
phrases: I usually start my day by
By the end of the day,
questions.sample: I usually start my day around seven with a quick walk. After that, I have breakfast and check my messages. Most of my day goes into work and learning new skills. In the evening, I relax with music or call my family. By the end of the day, I try to plan tomorrow's tasks.

questions.q: What did you do last weekend?
questions.tip: Use the past tense: went, met, watched, ate. Add one detail that makes it interesting.
questions.sample: Last weekend, I visited my cousin's place and we went out for lunch. The best part was trying a new biryani restaurant near Gachibowli. It was really relaxing after a busy week. Next weekend, I'm planning to stay home and finish a course I started.

questions.q: What are your hobbies and why do you enjoy them?
questions.tip: Name one or two hobbies and give a reason for each. Reasons make you sound interesting.
phrases: In my free time, I enjoy
What I love about it is
questions.sample: In my free time, I enjoy playing cricket and watching tech videos. What I love about cricket is the teamwork. It helps me stay active and clear my mind. Recently, I've started reading short business books too.

questions.q: Describe your hometown to someone who has never been there.
questions.tip: Talk about location, food, people and one famous place.
questions.sample: I'm from a small town near Vijayawada. It's known for its rivers, temples and spicy food. People there are friendly and close to each other. If you ever visit, you must try the local mango pickle. What I miss most is the peaceful mornings.

questions.q: What's a movie or series you watched recently? Would you recommend it?
questions.tip: Give a one-line story, what you liked, and who would enjoy it.
questions.sample: Recently, I watched a series about startup founders. It's about a small team trying to build an app with very little money. What I liked most was how they solved problems together. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes business or technology.

questions.q: How do you usually spend time with your family or friends?
questions.tip: Use 'usually', 'sometimes', 'once in a while' to show frequency.
questions.sample: We usually have dinner together and talk about our day. Once in a while, we go out to a movie or a family function. My favourite thing is our long weekend chats over tea. It brings us closer and helps me relax.

questions.q: Tell me about a place you'd love to travel to and why.
questions.tip: Use 'I'd love to' and 'because'. Talk about what you would do there.
questions.sample: I'd love to visit Japan, mainly because of its mix of technology and tradition. I'd like to see Tokyo's busy streets and also the quiet temples in Kyoto. I also want to try real Japanese food. It's on my list for the next few years.

questions.q: What's something new you learned this month?
questions.tip: Explain what you learned, how, and how you'll use it.
questions.sample: This month, I learned how to make simple presentations in Canva. I picked it up by watching short tutorials and practising every evening. It's useful because I can now explain my projects clearly. Next, I want to learn basic video editing.

questions.q: How do you handle stress on a busy day?
questions.tip: Give 2 or 3 real habits. Keep it practical.
questions.sample: When things get busy, I first write down everything I need to do. One thing that helps is doing the most important task first. I also try to take a short walk or a few deep breaths. That way, I stay calm and finish my work on time.

questions.q: Describe your favourite food and how it's made.
questions.tip: Use sequence words: first, then, next, finally.
questions.sample: My favourite food is chicken biryani. First, the chicken is marinated with curd and spices. Then, rice is cooked halfway with whole spices. Next, they're layered together and cooked slowly on low heat. Finally, it's served with raita. The smell alone makes me hungry.

models.name: Interview
models.about: Common HR and behavioural questions. Answer in 45 to 90 seconds.

questions.q: Tell me about yourself.
questions.tip: Present, past, future: who you are now, one or two achievements, why this role.
phrases: One thing I'm proud of is
questions.sample: Currently, I'm a computer science graduate focused on web development. Before this, I completed a six-month internship where I built features for a billing app. One thing I'm proud of is reducing the page load time by thirty percent. Now I'm looking for a role where I can grow as a developer and work with a strong team.

questions.q: What are your greatest strengths?
questions.tip: Pick two strengths and prove each with a quick example.
phrases: I believe this would help your team
questions.sample: My main strengths are problem solving and clear communication. For example, during my final project, I found the cause of a bug that the team had been stuck on for days. This helped us finish on time. I believe this would help your team deliver quality work.

questions.q: What is your biggest weakness?
questions.tip: Real but manageable, and show what you're doing to improve.
phrases: One area I'm working on is
questions.sample: One area I'm working on is public speaking. I've noticed that I get nervous in front of large groups. To improve, I practise short talks every day and take part in team meetings more often. I've already seen my confidence grow.

questions.q: Why do you want to work for our company?
questions.tip: Mention something specific about the company, then link it to your goals.
phrases: I see a chance to grow
questions.sample: I'm impressed by how your company builds products that millions of people use every day. It matches my interest in building useful, reliable software. I'd like to contribute my skills in web development, and I see a chance to grow by learning from an experienced team.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem.
questions.tip: Use STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Spend most time on Action.
questions.sample: The situation was that our app crashed for some users during a demo week. My task was to find the cause quickly. So I checked the logs, reproduced the error and found a database query that timed out. I rewrote it and added a test. As a result, the crashes stopped and the demo went smoothly.

questions.q: Where do you see yourself in five years?
questions.tip: Show ambition that fits the company: skills, responsibility, impact.
phrases: In five years, I see myself
questions.sample: In five years, I see myself as a senior developer who can lead small projects. I'd like to have strong skills in system design and mentoring. I hope to take more responsibility for product decisions, ideally here, growing with the company.

questions.q: Why should we hire you?
questions.tip: Skills they need, proof you have them, and your attitude.
questions.sample: You should hire me because I have the technical skills this role needs and I learn fast. I've already built and deployed real projects, including an internship app used by real customers. I'm also a good team player who communicates clearly. I'm confident that I can add value from the first month.

questions.q: Tell me about a time you worked in a team.
questions.tip: Say 'I' for your part and 'we' for the team result.
questions.sample: We were a team of four building a college event app. My role was the backend and connecting it to the mobile screens. I made sure everyone knew what the others were doing with short daily updates. Together, we finished a week early and the app handled over five hundred users.

questions.q: What are your salary expectations?
questions.tip: Give a researched range and show you're flexible.
questions.sample: Based on my research for similar roles in this city, I'm expecting a range of six to seven lakhs per year. I'm open to discussing it, as I'm also interested in the learning opportunities and the overall package.

questions.q: Do you have any questions for us?
questions.tip: Always ask one or two good questions about the team, success or next steps.
questions.sample: Yes, I'd like to know more about the team I'd be working with. What would success look like in the first six months? And could you tell me about the next steps in the process?

models.name: Presentation
models.about: Opening, explaining and closing a talk with clear structure.

questions.q: Open a presentation about your final-year project.
questions.tip: Greet, introduce yourself, say the topic and what you'll cover.
phrases: Today, I'm going to talk about
questions.sample: Good morning, everyone. My name is Ravi. Today, I'm going to talk about our final-year project, a smart attendance system. I'll cover three things: the problem, how our solution works, and the results. Let's begin with the problem.

questions.q: Explain a chart that shows sales growing over the year.
questions.tip: Describe the trend, the key numbers, and what it means.
questions.sample: As you can see, sales grew throughout the year. There's a steady increase from January to June, and the biggest jump was in October, during the festival season, when sales rose by forty percent. This shows that our festival campaigns work well.

questions.q: Move from one section of your talk to the next.
questions.tip: Use transition phrases so the audience knows where you are.
questions.sample: Now that we've seen the problem, let's move on to our solution. This brings me to the main part of the project. Next, I'd like to show you how the app works step by step.

questions.q: Close your presentation and invite questions.
questions.tip: Summarise the key points, give a final message, then invite questions.
phrases: I'm happy to take any questions.
questions.sample: To sum up, our system saves teachers about ten minutes per class and reduces errors in attendance. The key takeaway is that small automation can save a lot of time. Thank you for listening. I'm happy to take any questions.

questions.q: Answer a question you don't fully know during a presentation.
questions.tip: Be honest, share what you do know, and offer to follow up.
phrases: I don't have the exact figure
What I can tell you is
I'll check and get back to you
questions.sample: That's a great question. I don't have the exact figure with me right now. What I can tell you is that the trend has been positive over the last three months. I'll check the details and get back to you by tomorrow.

questions.q: Introduce a new idea to your team in a short pitch.
questions.tip: Problem, idea, benefit, next step. Keep it under a minute.
questions.sample: I'd like to suggest a weekly fifteen-minute demo session. Right now, we often don't know what other teams are building. This would help us share ideas and avoid repeated work. As a first step, we could try it for one month and see how it goes.

questions.q: Give a one-minute update on a project's progress.
questions.tip: Done, in progress, blockers, next steps.
questions.sample: Here's a quick update. So far, we've finished the login and payment screens. We're currently working on notifications, which should be ready by Friday. One challenge is a delay from the design team, but we've planned around it. Next week, we'll start testing.

questions.q: Explain a technical idea to someone who isn't technical.
questions.tip: Use a simple comparison from daily life.
questions.sample: In simple terms, the cloud is like renting storage instead of buying your own cupboard. Think of it like keeping your files in a safe locker that you can open from anywhere. For example, you can see your photos on your phone and laptop. The benefit for you is that nothing is lost if your phone breaks.

questions.q: Recover after making a small mistake on a slide.
questions.tip: Stay calm, correct it simply, and move on.
questions.sample: Sorry, let me correct that. That should say twenty percent, not two percent. Thanks for your patience. Moving on, the next slide shows how we reached that number.

questions.q: Tell a short story to begin a talk about teamwork.
questions.tip: A short real moment hooks the audience. Then connect it to your topic.
phrases: Let me start with a quick story.
And that's what today's talk is about.
questions.sample: Let me start with a quick story. In my first internship, our whole server went down an hour before a client demo. At that moment, nobody blamed anyone; everyone just picked a task. We fixed it with ten minutes to spare. What I learned was that trust makes teams fast. And that's what today's talk is about.

models.name: Group discussion
models.about: Starting, joining, agreeing, disagreeing and summarising in a group.

questions.q: Start a group discussion on: Should work from home continue?
questions.tip: Define the topic, give both sides briefly, and share your view.
questions.sample: I'd like to start by saying that work from home changed how we see offices. On one hand, it saves travel time and gives flexibility. On the other hand, some people feel lonely and teamwork can suffer. In my opinion, a hybrid model, with two or three office days, works best.

questions.q: Politely join a discussion when others keep talking.
questions.tip: Wait for a small pause, then enter with a polite phrase.
phrases: If I may add a point,
questions.sample: If I may add a point, I think we're missing the cost side. Building on what Priya said, companies also save on office space with remote work, which is a big benefit.

questions.q: Agree with someone and add a new point.
questions.tip: Agree, then add something new so you don't just repeat.
questions.sample: I completely agree with Arjun, and I'd also add that online learning helps people in small towns. Another example is students who can now attend courses from top universities. That's why I think the benefits are bigger than the problems.

questions.q: Disagree politely with a point in the discussion.
questions.tip: Respect the person, then give your reason and an example.
questions.sample: I see your point, but I'm not sure I agree that social media only harms students. The reason is that many students use it to learn and network. For instance, I found my internship through LinkedIn.

questions.q: Bring a group back to the topic when it goes off track.
questions.tip: Be polite and remind everyone of the main question.
questions.sample: That's interesting, but let's come back to the main topic. The main question is whether AI will create more jobs than it removes. So, coming back to that, I think it will create new kinds of jobs, like AI trainers and reviewers.

questions.q: Summarise a group discussion at the end.
questions.tip: Mention the main views fairly, then the overall conclusion.
questions.sample: To summarise, we discussed whether electric vehicles are ready for India. Some of us felt that cost and charging points are still a problem, while others believed government support will solve this soon. Overall, we agreed that electric vehicles are the future, but the change will take a few years.

questions.q: Give your view on: Is social media good for youth?
questions.tip: Clear opinion, two reasons, one example.
questions.sample: I believe that social media is good for youth if it's used wisely. Firstly, it helps young people learn new skills for free. Secondly, it connects them to opportunities and people. For example, many students build portfolios and get freelance work online. The key is to limit time and avoid comparison.

questions.q: Invite a quiet member of the group to speak.
questions.tip: Including others shows leadership in a GD.
phrases: I'd love to hear your view
questions.sample: We haven't heard from Meera yet. What do you think about this, Meera? I'd love to hear your view on whether exams should be fully online. Please go ahead.

questions.q: Respond when someone challenges your point strongly.
questions.tip: Stay calm, accept what's fair, and support your point with a fact.
questions.sample: That's a fair point, and I agree cost is a concern. However, according to recent reports, solar panel prices have dropped by more than half in ten years. So I still feel solar energy is a practical choice for most homes.

questions.q: Give your view on: Should college education be free?
questions.tip: Show you can see both sides, then decide.
questions.sample: This is a complex issue. The benefit would be that talented students from poor families get equal chances. But we must consider who pays for it and how to keep quality high. A middle path could be free education for low-income students and scholarships for merit.

models.name: Convincing people
models.about: Persuading with reasons, benefits and examples, without pressure.

questions.q: Convince your manager to let you work from home two days a week.
questions.tip: Focus on benefits for the team, offer a trial, show you'll stay reachable.
phrases: This would help the team because
Could we try it for a month?
questions.sample: I'd like to propose working from home two days a week. This would help the team because I'd save two hours of travel and use that time for focused work. I'll make sure I'm available on calls and finish my tasks on time. Could we try it for a month and review it together?

questions.q: Convince a friend to start exercising.
questions.tip: Make it easy and personal. Offer to join them.
questions.sample: Have you thought about starting a short walk in the mornings? Even twenty minutes a day can improve your energy and sleep. You'll notice you feel less tired at work within a couple of weeks. Why don't we start together this Monday?

questions.q: Convince a customer to try your product.
questions.tip: Understand their problem, show the benefit, reduce the risk.
phrases: What makes our product different is
You can try it free for
questions.sample: I understand that you need something simple and affordable. What makes our product different is that it's easy to set up in ten minutes. Many of our customers saved hours every week after switching. You can try it free for fourteen days, with no card needed.

questions.q: Convince your team to use a new tool.
questions.tip: Show the current problem, the benefit, and make the change small.
phrases: Let's try it on one project first
questions.sample: Right now, we spend a lot of time searching for files in long email threads. This tool would keep all our tasks and files in one place. It's easy to learn, and I can show everyone in a fifteen-minute session. Let's try it on one project first and decide after two weeks.

questions.q: Convince your parents about a career choice they're unsure of.
questions.tip: Respect their worry, give facts, and show your plan.
questions.sample: I understand your concern about job security. Let me explain why I want to work in design. Companies now hire designers for every app and website, and salaries are growing. My plan is to finish a certified course and build a portfolio within six months. I'll keep you updated on my progress.

questions.q: Ask for a deadline extension and convince the client.
questions.tip: Be honest about the reason, show progress, give a new firm date.
phrases: To make sure the quality is right,
questions.sample: I wanted to update you on the project. We've completed eighty percent of the work, including all main screens. To make sure the quality is right, we need three more days for testing. We can deliver by Thursday, and I'll share daily updates until then.

questions.q: Convince someone to join your volunteer event.
questions.tip: Make it meaningful and easy to say yes to.
phrases: Would you like to join us?
questions.sample: We're organising a beach clean-up this Sunday morning. It's a great chance to help the city and meet some nice people. It only takes three hours, and we'll provide gloves and breakfast. Would you like to join us?

questions.q: Convince an interviewer you can learn a skill you don't have yet.
questions.tip: Admit it, show a similar thing you learned fast, and give a plan.
phrases: I haven't used it yet, but
questions.sample: I haven't used that tool yet, but I learn new tools quickly. Last year, I learned React within three weeks and used it in a live project. My plan would be to complete the official tutorial in my first week and build a small feature with guidance.

questions.q: Convince a group to choose your idea for a college fest.
questions.tip: Compare options fairly and show why yours fits best.
questions.sample: I'd suggest a startup pitch competition. Compared to a regular quiz, it's more exciting and attracts sponsors. It's also great for students who want to build businesses. If we go with this, I can contact two local startup founders to be judges.

questions.q: Convince a shopkeeper to give you a better price.
questions.tip: Be friendly, give a reason, and offer something in return.
questions.sample: I really like this jacket, but it's a little above my budget. Is there any discount you can offer? If I buy two items today, could you do it for three thousand instead of three and a half?

models.name: Polite declining
models.about: Saying no kindly and clearly, while keeping the relationship good.

questions.q: Decline extra work from your manager because you're already busy.
questions.tip: Show you're willing, explain the clash, offer a choice.
phrases: I'd really like to help, but
questions.sample: I'd really like to help, but right now I'm working on the client report due tomorrow. If I take this on, the report might get delayed. Could we look at it on Friday instead? Or, which one should I prioritise?

questions.q: Decline a friend's party invitation.
questions.tip: Thank them, give a short reason, suggest another time.
phrases: Thanks so much for inviting me.
I hope you have a great time.
questions.sample: Thanks so much for inviting me. Unfortunately, I have a family function that evening, so I can't make it. I hope you have a great time. Let's catch up for coffee next week.

questions.q: Decline a job offer politely.
questions.tip: Thank them, give a brief reason, and keep the door open.
phrases: I hope our paths cross again
questions.sample: Thank you for the offer and for your time during the process. After careful thought, I've decided to accept another role that's closer to my long-term goals. I really appreciated meeting your team, and I hope our paths cross again.

questions.q: Say no when a colleague asks to borrow money.
questions.tip: Be kind but firm. You don't need a long excuse.
phrases: I'm sorry, I'm not able to
Is there anything else I can help with?
questions.sample: I'm sorry, I'm not able to lend money right now. I have some commitments of my own this month. I hope you understand. Is there anything else I can help with?

questions.q: Decline a sales call politely.
questions.tip: Short and clear. No need to explain much.
questions.sample: Thanks for calling, but I'm not interested in a new credit card at the moment. Please remove my number from your list. Have a good day.

questions.q: Turn down a meeting that you don't need to attend.
questions.tip: Offer an alternative so you still help.
phrases: I don't think I'm needed for
I'm happy to give input by
questions.sample: Thanks for including me. I don't think I'm needed for the full meeting, since my part is only the budget. Could you share the notes afterwards? I'm happy to give input by email before the meeting.

questions.q: Decline a request from your relative to fix their computer this weekend.
questions.tip: Show care and suggest another way.
questions.sample: I wish I could, but this weekend I'm preparing for an interview. How about I help you on Tuesday evening? Meanwhile, you could try restarting it once; that often solves the problem.

questions.q: Refuse an unfair request from a client.
questions.tip: Stay professional, explain the limit, and offer what you can do.
questions.sample: I understand why you're asking for the extra features. However, that's outside the scope we agreed on for this price. What I can do is add them as a second phase with a separate quote. Would that work for you?

questions.q: Say no to a friend who wants to copy your assignment.
questions.tip: Be honest and kind, and offer real help instead.
questions.sample: I can't share my work, because we'd both get into trouble if it's caught. But I'm happy to explain the topic to you. Shall we sit together for half an hour tomorrow?

questions.q: Decline a promotion that would mean moving to another city.
questions.tip: Show gratitude, give your reason, and show continued commitment.
phrases: I'd love to be considered for
questions.sample: I'm honoured to be considered for this role. At this point, I need to stay in Hyderabad for family reasons, so I'm not able to move. I'm still very committed to growing in the company, and I'd love to be considered for future roles here.

models.name: Small talk & networking
models.about: Starting conversations, introducing yourself and keeping a chat going.

questions.q: Introduce yourself to someone at a networking event.
questions.tip: Name, what you do, one interesting detail, then ask about them.
questions.sample: Hi, I'm Ravi. Nice to meet you. I work in web development, mostly building business apps. I'm here to learn more about startups. What brings you here?

questions.q: Start a conversation with a new colleague on their first day.
questions.tip: Welcome them and offer help. Ask an easy question.
questions.sample: Welcome to the team! I'm Ravi from the design side. How's your first day going? If you need anything, like finding the meeting rooms, just ask me. Have you had lunch yet? Some of us go at one o'clock.

questions.q: Keep a conversation going when it becomes quiet.
questions.tip: Ask open questions starting with what, how or why.
phrases: What do you enjoy most about
questions.sample: By the way, how did you get into data science? That sounds interesting. What do you enjoy most about your work?

questions.q: Talk about the weather in a natural way.
questions.tip: Comment, add a personal note, and pass the conversation back.
phrases: I love this kind of weather
questions.sample: It's really pleasant today, isn't it? I love this kind of weather after all that heat. Do you prefer the rainy season or winter?

questions.q: End a conversation politely at an event.
questions.tip: Show you enjoyed it, give a reason to leave, suggest staying in touch.
phrases: It was great talking to you.
Can I connect with you on LinkedIn?
questions.sample: It was great talking to you. I should go and say hello to my manager before she leaves. Let's stay in touch. Can I connect with you on LinkedIn?

questions.q: Ask a senior person for career advice.
questions.tip: Be respectful, specific and brief.
phrases: If you don't mind me asking,
questions.sample: I really admire how you moved from development into product management. If you don't mind me asking, what would you recommend for someone who wants to make the same move? Thank you, that's really helpful.

questions.q: Chat with a stranger while waiting in a long queue.
questions.tip: A light, friendly comment is enough to start.
phrases: Looks like we'll be here a while!
questions.sample: Looks like we'll be here a while! Have you been to this office before? I've heard the afternoon is usually quieter. Anyway, good luck with your work today.

questions.q: Compliment someone's work in a natural way.
questions.tip: Be specific about what you liked.
questions.sample: I really liked your presentation today, especially the part where you showed the customer journey. It was very clear. How did you prepare those visuals? Great job.

questions.q: Respond when someone asks 'How are you?' at work.
questions.tip: Give a short real answer and ask back.
questions.sample: I'm doing well, thanks. It's been a busy week with the product launch, but it's going smoothly. How about you? Any plans for the weekend?

questions.q: Follow up with someone you met at an event.
questions.tip: Remind them where you met and suggest a next step.
phrases: It was nice meeting you at
questions.sample: Hi Anil, it was nice meeting you at the tech meetup on Saturday. I enjoyed our chat about AI tools for small businesses. I'd love to learn more about your work. Would you be free for a short call next week?

models.name: Phone & video calls
models.about: Office calls: opening, explaining, handling bad connections and closing.

questions.q: Start a work call with a client you haven't met.
questions.tip: Greet, introduce yourself, confirm the purpose and time.
phrases: Is this still a good time?
questions.sample: Hello, this is Ravi from Bright Solutions. Thanks for taking the time to speak with me. I'm calling about the website project we discussed by email. Is this still a good time for about fifteen minutes?

questions.q: Ask someone to repeat because the connection is bad.
questions.tip: Polite and clear. Suggest a fix if it continues.
phrases: I didn't catch the last part.
questions.sample: Sorry, you're breaking up a little. Could you repeat that? I didn't catch the last part about the delivery date. If it continues, shall I call you back?

questions.q: Leave a voicemail for a recruiter.
questions.tip: Name, reason, number twice, best time to call.
phrases: Thank you, and have a good day.
questions.sample: Hi, this is Ravi Kumar. I'm calling about the software developer role I applied for last week. You can reach me at 98765 43210, that's 98765 43210. I'm available after two pm. Thank you, and have a good day.

questions.q: Explain a delay to a customer on a call.
questions.tip: Apologise, explain simply, give the new date and what you're doing.
questions.sample: I'm sorry for the delay with your order. The reason is a shortage at our warehouse this week. Your order will now arrive on Friday. I'll personally make sure it's shipped first thing tomorrow, and you'll get a tracking message.

questions.q: End a video meeting with next steps.
questions.tip: Summarise decisions, owners and dates.
questions.sample: Before we finish, let me confirm the next steps. So, to confirm, Priya will share the design by Wednesday, and I'll send the cost estimate by Thursday. We'll meet again next Monday. Thanks, everyone.

questions.q: Ask your manager for a quick call to discuss a problem.
questions.tip: Say what it's about and how long you need.
questions.sample: Hi, do you have ten minutes today? I'd like to discuss an issue with the payment feature. It's about a bug that might affect the release date. Whenever suits you is fine.

questions.q: Handle a call when you're not the right person to help.
questions.tip: Be helpful: take details or connect them to the right person.
phrases: I'm not the right person for that,
May I take your name and number?
questions.sample: I'm not the right person for billing questions, but I can connect you to our accounts team. May I take your name and number? Someone from accounts will call you back within an hour.

questions.q: Share your screen and walk someone through a document.
questions.tip: Tell them what they should see and guide them step by step.
questions.sample: I'm sharing my screen now. Can you see the spreadsheet? If you look at the first column, you'll see the monthly totals. Let me scroll down to the summary at the bottom.

questions.q: Join a meeting late and apologise briefly.
questions.tip: Short apology, no long story, then focus.
phrases: I'll catch up from the notes.
questions.sample: Sorry I'm late, everyone. I was stuck in another call that ran over. Please carry on; I'll catch up from the notes.

questions.q: Confirm details at the end of a phone call.
questions.tip: Repeat the key details to avoid mistakes.
questions.sample: Just to confirm, the interview is on Tuesday the twenty-fifth at eleven am, at your Hitech City office. So that's Tuesday at eleven. Is that correct?

models.name: Opinions & debates
models.about: Giving opinions with reasons, comparing options and reaching a view.

questions.q: Is it better to work at a startup or a big company?
questions.tip: Compare two or three points fairly, then choose.
questions.sample: Both have advantages. At a startup, you learn many things quickly and get more responsibility, whereas at a big company, you get stability, structure and good training. Personally, I'd choose a big company first to build strong basics, and then move to a startup.

questions.q: Should mobile phones be allowed in classrooms?
questions.tip: Opinion, reason, example, conclusion.
questions.sample: In my view, phones should be allowed only for learning activities, because they can be useful but also distracting. For example, students can use apps for quizzes, but social media during class hurts focus. So overall, I support clear rules rather than a full ban.

questions.q: Will AI take away jobs?
questions.tip: Show balance and give a realistic view.
questions.sample: It's true that AI will replace some repetitive jobs. However, it will also create new roles, like AI trainers and data specialists. History shows that new technology usually changes jobs more than it removes them. I think the key is to keep learning new skills.

questions.q: What's more important: salary or job satisfaction?
questions.tip: Explain how your answer might change over time.
questions.sample: For me, job satisfaction matters more, because I spend most of my day at work. That said, salary is important at the start of a career to support my family. In the long run, I believe enjoying my work will also lead to better pay.

questions.q: Should people read books or watch videos to learn?
questions.tip: Compare and suggest when each one works best.
questions.sample: It depends on what you're learning. Books are better for deep understanding and focus, while videos are great for practical skills like cooking or coding. Ideally, we should use both: videos to start and books to go deeper.

questions.q: Is online shopping better than going to shops?
questions.tip: Use a personal example to make your opinion real.
questions.sample: I prefer online shopping, mainly because it saves time and I can compare prices easily. On the other hand, shops let you touch and try things. For things like clothes and shoes, I still like going to a store.

questions.q: Should everyone learn to code?
questions.tip: Give a clear yes, no or 'partly', with reasons.
questions.sample: I'd say not everyone needs to become a programmer, but everyone can benefit from basic coding. It teaches logical thinking and problem solving. For instance, simple automation can save office workers hours every week.

questions.q: Is it better to live in a big city or a small town?
questions.tip: Compare cost, opportunities and lifestyle.
questions.sample: Living in a big city gives you more jobs, better colleges and more things to do, but it's expensive and stressful. A small town is calmer and cheaper. If I had to choose, I'd live in a city while building my career and move to a smaller place later.

questions.q: Should students take a gap year before college?
questions.tip: Talk about who it suits and how to use it well.
phrases: A gap year can be useful if
questions.sample: A gap year can be useful if students use it to work, travel or explore interests. However, without a plan, it can become a wasted year. The important thing is to set clear goals. In my opinion, it's a good idea for students who are unsure about their career.

questions.q: Is failure necessary for success?
questions.tip: Share a personal example of learning from failure.
questions.sample: I strongly believe failure is part of success. When I failed my first coding test, I felt bad, but I learned that I needed to practise problem solving every day. Three months later, I cleared a much harder test. That's why I see failure as feedback.

models.name: Tough moments
models.about: Apologising, admitting mistakes, asking for clarification and saying 'I don't know' well.

questions.q: Apologise to your manager for missing a deadline.
questions.tip: Own it, explain briefly, give the fix and how you'll prevent it.
questions.sample: I'm sorry I missed the deadline for the report. It was my mistake; I underestimated the data cleaning work. I'll have it ready by tomorrow at noon. In future, I'll share progress earlier if I see any risk.

questions.q: Ask your manager to explain an instruction you didn't understand.
questions.tip: Repeat what you understood and ask about the unclear part.
phrases: Just to make sure I understand,
questions.sample: Just to make sure I understand, you'd like me to update the sales sheet every Friday. Could you clarify whether I should include online orders too? Thanks, that's clear now.

questions.q: Answer an interview question you don't know the answer to.
questions.tip: Be honest, show how you'd find the answer, and share related knowledge.
phrases: but here's how I'd approach it.
I'd be keen to learn more
questions.sample: I'm not sure about the exact details of that algorithm, but here's how I'd approach it. I'd first look at the input size and the time limits. I do know that a hash map would make the lookups much faster. I'd be keen to learn more about it.

questions.q: Respond to an angry customer complaint.
questions.tip: Listen, acknowledge the feeling, apologise and give action.
questions.sample: I'm really sorry about the wrong item in your order. I understand how frustrating that must be. Here's what I'll do: I'll arrange a free pickup today and send the correct item by express delivery. You'll hear from me by this evening with the tracking details.

questions.q: Give negative feedback to a teammate kindly.
questions.tip: Start positive, be specific about the issue, suggest a solution.
phrases: You've done a great job on
questions.sample: You've done a great job on the new design. One thing I noticed is that some screens take a while to load on older phones. It might help to compress the images. What do you think?

questions.q: Receive criticism from your manager calmly.
questions.tip: Thank them, accept it, and say what you'll change.
questions.sample: Thank you for telling me. You're right that my emails to the client were too long. From now on, I'll keep them short with clear points. Could you check the next one before I send it?

questions.q: Correct someone politely when they've made a mistake.
questions.tip: Be gentle and give the right information.
phrases: Sorry, I think there might be
questions.sample: Sorry, I think there might be a small mistake in the invoice. Actually, the total should be twelve thousand, not fifteen. Just checking so we don't confuse the client. Thanks!

questions.q: Ask for help when you're stuck at work.
questions.tip: Show what you've tried and ask a specific question.
questions.sample: I'm stuck on connecting the app to the payment gateway. I've already tried the documentation steps and checked the keys. Could you point me in the right direction? I'd really appreciate it.

questions.q: Explain a gap in your resume in an interview.
questions.tip: Be honest and positive, and show what you did during the gap.
questions.sample: During that time, I was taking care of a family member who was unwell. I also focused on learning, completing two online courses in data analysis. It helped me become more organised and patient. Now I'm ready to return to full-time work.

questions.q: Say 'I don't know' in a meeting without sounding unprepared.
questions.tip: Admit it and promise a clear follow-up.
phrases: I don't have that answer right now,
questions.sample: Good question. I don't have that answer right now, but I'll find out from the finance team and share it by the end of the day.
